title: Deuteronomy 1:9–18
context: Moses recalls how Israel’s growth made it impossible for him to lead and judge them alone. At his suggestion, the people chose wise and respected men from each tribe, whom he appointed as leaders and judges. He charged them to judge fairly, without partiality or fear, because judgment belongs to God.

verses.text: I spoke to you at that time, saying, “I am not able to bear you myself alone.
verses.arminianNotes: Moses admits he cannot carry the people alone. Leadership in God’s community is meant to be shared. Exodus 18 and Numbers 11 describe related moments.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note the same humility and the same cross-references. This is shared ground.

verses.text: The LORD your God has multiplied you, and behold, you are today as the stars of the sky for multitude.
verses.arminianNotes: Israel has become as numerous as the stars, echoing God’s promise to Abraham (Genesis 15:5). The burden Moses feels is the result of God’s blessing.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers also see the fulfillment of the Abrahamic promise. This is shared ground.

verses.text: May the LORD, the God of your fathers, make you a thousand times as many as you are and bless you, as he has promised you!
verses.arminianNotes: Moses blesses the people and prays that God would multiply them a thousand times more. He does not resent their growth; he welcomes it.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers read this as a pastor’s blessing grounded in God’s promise. This is shared ground.

verses.text: How can I myself alone bear your problems, your burdens, and your strife?
verses.arminianNotes: Moses names the problems, burdens, and strife that come with a large community. Conflict is a normal part of life together, and it needs structure.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree that God provides order for the life of his people. This is shared ground.

verses.text: Take wise men of understanding who are respected among your tribes, and I will make them heads over you.”
verses.arminianNotes: The people are to choose wise, understanding, respected men, and Moses will appoint them. Character comes before position.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note the same priority on character, echoed in New Testament qualifications for leaders (1 Timothy 3; Titus 1). This is shared ground.

verses.text: You answered me, and said, “The thing which you have spoken is good to do.”
verses.arminianNotes: The people agree that the plan is good. The appointment of leaders is a shared act of the community.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers read this the same way. This is shared ground.

verses.text: So I took the heads of your tribes, wise and respected men, and made them heads over you, captains of thousands, captains of hundreds, captains of fifties, captains of tens, and officers, according to your tribes.
verses.arminianNotes: Moses appoints leaders over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens. The structure allows each person to be cared for.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see orderly, layered leadership. This is shared ground.

verses.text: I commanded your judges at that time, saying, “Hear cases between your brothers and judge righteously between a man and his brother, and the foreigner who is living with him.
verses.arminianNotes: Judges must hear cases fairly, including those involving foreigners. Justice belongs to everyone in the community.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note the same concern for impartial justice, including for the vulnerable. This is shared ground.

verses.text: You shall not show partiality in judgment; you shall hear the small and the great alike. You shall not be afraid of the face of man, for the judgment is God’s. The case that is too hard for you, you shall bring to me, and I will hear it.”
verses.arminianNotes: No partiality, no fear of people, “for the judgment is God’s.” Judges act as God’s servants and answer to him. Hard cases go up to Moses.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers emphasize the same ground: human judges represent God’s justice. James 2:1–9 applies the ban on partiality to the church. This is shared ground.

verses.text: I commanded you at that time all the things which you should do.
verses.arminianNotes: Moses commanded them all they should do. The new generation is reminded that God’s instructions were given clearly.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree. This is shared ground.
